anti_patterns: Do not use the seal as Ateles's logo, hero object, or primary metaphor. It is only a secondary state marker for a concrete authorization, commitment, approval, or completed checkpoint.
Do not literalize “swarm” with monkeys, spiders, insects, hives, honeycombs, or mascot clusters. Show a living collective through abstract named roles and relationships.
Do not render an anonymous neural-network mesh. Every visible node or path must communicate an organizational role, relationship, handoff, priority, or intervention state.

Never expose internal record IDs, entity types, field or decision keys, code-call names, repository filenames, phase bookkeeping, agent instructions, or bracketed internal scope notation on a public page.
Do not paste research analysis, source citations, or implementation-review notes into public prose. Preserve evidence in linked source artifacts and translate it into concise reader-facing claims.
Do not let motion carry organizational meaning that disappears under reduced-motion preferences; the static graph must remain legible and complete.
Do not spread authorization or withdrawal colors as general accents; reserve them for active versus withdrawn, expired, or paused authority.
Do not diverge shared structural tokens from Neotoma without a product reason; the products remain siblings through spacing, restraint, and hierarchy.
Do not reuse the Neotoma app or Inspector palette. Ateles keeps its warm paper and ink system with a rust coordination accent.

positioning_principles: Organizational properties become visual stories rather than implementation prose: named roles are differentiated swarm members; coordinated execution appears as temporary signals and short handoffs; priority context is a mission-to-task sequence; intervention points are explicit checkpoints.

Swarm (primary symbol): an abstract constellation of distinct, semi-autonomous roles coordinating through motion, proximity, signals, and temporary handoffs around shared purpose. The mark remains recognizable at navigation size and expands into a cinematic field without permanent connecting edges or a central hub.

The swarm names Ateles-specific collective behavior; the organization is the product promise. The visual feels coordinated and adaptive, while authority, governance, and accountability provide the structure that makes the collective trustworthy.

Swarm before authority marker: differentiated members and their temporary coordination carry brand recognition. A small seal appears only beside a concrete authorization, commitment, approval, or completed checkpoint; it annotates state and never becomes the logo or hero object.

Public labels use ordinary organizational language: role, responsibility, scope, handoff, current priority, needs review, approved, and paused. Never display internal IDs, entity types, decision keys, repository filenames, code-call names, phase bookkeeping, or unexplained product vocabulary.

Coordination rhythm: proximity, differentiated shapes, restrained member motion, and short-lived signals show work passing between accountable roles. Static reduced-motion views preserve clustering, role difference, shared direction, and checkpoints without drawing a permanent graph.

Approval and escalation appear as structural proof: a temporary handoff pauses at a bounded checkpoint, a consequential decision returns to the operator, and collective action visibly resumes. Phrase thresholds in plain language.

Color is semantic: rust marks active but temporary coordination signals; green marks an active authorization or resolved checkpoint; withdrawn or paused states stay visually separate. Avoid ambient seal washes and generic SaaS gradients.

Hero cinema is the preferred primary medium once the visual semantics are correct: a silent 6–10 second loop should show autonomous differentiated members self-organizing, exchanging work through temporary signals, pausing at one bounded checkpoint, and continuing—without permanent edges, a central hub, literal creatures, robots, hives, honeycomb, or anonymous neural mesh. Until that replacement exists, the code-native swarm takeover is primary and the current connected-node film remains exploratory only.
identity.scope: Ateles product pages only (distinct from the shared structural design system, which this identity does not replace). The primary symbol is a swarm: many distinct, semi-autonomous human and agent roles coordinating around shared work and mission. Render it as an abstract, differentiated node-and-path mark that remains recognizable in the navigation and expands into a richer organization network in the hero. Never use literal insects, monkeys, spiders, hives, honeycomb, or an anonymous neural-network mesh. The organization is the public product promise; authority and governance are the structure that makes coordinated action legitimate. The authorization seal is secondary: a compact state marker applied only to a specific grant, commitment, approval, or completed checkpoint. Ateles remains a sibling, not a twin, of Neotoma: shared spacing and restraint, different symbolic grammar.

color_palette.rationale: Swarm coordination, not wax-seal brand theater: the warm paper and ink base makes the system feel inhabited and legible, while rust traces relationships, handoffs, and directed motion among differentiated roles. Green remains semantic and reserved for active authorization; revoked remains reserved for withdrawn or expired authority. A small seal survives only as a secondary state marker attached to an authorization, commitment, or completed checkpoint—not as the product symbol or ambient palette rationale.

type_scale.google_fonts_licence: All three (Space Grotesk, Source Sans 3, IBM Plex Mono) are free, open-license Google Fonts already loaded via the current font mechanism; no licensing action is needed.
type_scale.rationale: Family kept deliberately: research checked 2026-09-21 (typewolf.com/space-grotesk and madegooddesigns.com/space-grotesk-font) found Space Grotesk broadly signals forward-looking technology rather than authority by itself. The identity therefore comes from the living organization visual, not from inventing a more authoritative typeface. IBM Plex Mono is reserved for short, plain-language role, scope, handoff, priority, and status labels. It must not carry internal bracketed scope formats, IDs, decision keys, code vocabulary, or phase bookkeeping.
